title: Line + dot together, sonar, llegué, me quedé, me gustó / me gustaba, me pareció

cards.title: Line and dot together
cards.body: 'I was cooking' is the line (background); 'the phone rang' is the dot (event). Teléfono is Greek: tele (far) + phone (voice). Sonar = to sound / ring.

examples.en: I was cooking when the phone rang.

cards.title: llegué, llegó; por teléfono
cards.body: Por can also mean 'by': por teléfono = on the phone.

examples.en: I arrived / he arrived / we arrived
I was on the phone when María arrived.
examples.es: Hablaba por teléfono cuando llegó María.

examples.en: I stayed / she stayed / we stayed
examples.es: me quedé / se quedó / nos quedamos

cards.title: me gustó vs me gustaba
cards.body: 'It pleased me' = me gustó (me gusté = I liked myself). Both past forms can work: gustó treats it as a closed event, gustaba as ongoing. English never says 'I wasn't liking it', so don't look for direct translations.

examples.es: No me gustó. / No me gustaba.

cards.title: me pareció / me parecía
cards.body: Related to apparent, aparecer (to appear) and transparent.

examples.en: It seemed fine, but when I saw it I didn't like it.
examples.es: Me parecía bien, pero cuando lo vi no me gustó.

practice.en: I was cooking when the phone rang.
I was on the phone when María arrived.
es: Hablaba por teléfono cuando llegó María

practice.en: … but when I saw it, I didn't like it.
